findings.title: Removing more stock than available underflows the quantity
findings.explanation: The function subtracts without checking that enough stock exists. Unsigned subtraction panics in debug builds and wraps to a huge quantity in release builds.
findings.failure_scenario: If SKU A has quantity 3, calling remove_stock("A", 4) either panics or changes its quantity to 4,294,967,295.

findings.title: Average price accumulation can overflow
findings.explanation: Summing prices into u64 is unchecked. When the total exceeds u64::MAX, averaging either panics or uses a wrapped total.
findings.failure_scenario: An inventory containing two items each priced at u64::MAX causes average_price() to panic in debug builds and return an incorrect wrapped average in release builds.

findings.title: Calculating the average price of an empty inventory panics
findings.explanation: An empty inventory has length zero, so this integer division panics instead of producing a usable result or explicitly reporting that no average exists.
findings.failure_scenario: Calling Inventory::new().average_price() panics with an attempt to divide by zero.

findings.title: Top-value ranking overflows when calculating line values
findings.explanation: The sort key multiplies price by quantity without overflow handling. Overflow either panics or wraps, and wrapping can place the most valuable line below cheaper lines.
findings.failure_scenario: An item priced at u64::MAX with quantity 2 causes top_by_value(1) to panic in debug builds; in release its wrapped key can make the method return a less valuable item.

findings.title: Requesting more top items than exist panics
findings.explanation: The slice operation assumes n is no greater than the number of items, but the public method performs no such check.
findings.failure_scenario: With one inventory item, top_by_value(2) panics because the slice endpoint exceeds the vector length.

findings.title: Discount percentages above 100 underflow the result

anchor.snippet:
let discount = price_pence * percent_off as u64 / 100;
    price_pence - discount

findings.explanation: No range check limits percent_off to 100, so the computed discount can exceed the original price and the unsigned subtraction underflows.
findings.failure_scenario: apply_discount(100, 101) panics in debug builds and wraps to u64::MAX in release builds rather than returning a meaningful discounted price.

findings.title: Basket total overflows for large valid prices and quantities

anchor.snippet: let gross = unit_price_pence * quantity as u64;

findings.explanation: The gross total is computed with unchecked u64 multiplication. Large but type-valid inputs panic with overflow checks enabled and silently wrap otherwise.
findings.failure_scenario: basket_total(u64::MAX, 2) panics in debug builds; in release it wraps the gross to u64::MAX - 1 and calculates a nonsensical total.

findings.title: Bulk discounts are not applied at their documented thresholds
findings.explanation: The documented discount starts at 10 or 50 items, but strict comparisons exclude those exact boundary quantities.
findings.failure_scenario: A basket of 10 items receives 0% instead of 5%, and a basket of 50 items receives 5% instead of 10%.

findings.title: Price parsing panics on invalid input and misinterprets one-digit fractions
findings.explanation: The parser unwraps both the decimal separator and integer conversions, making ordinary malformed input a process panic. It also treats the fractional portion as raw pence rather than two decimal digits.
findings.failure_scenario: parse_price("12") or parse_price("12.xx") panics; parse_price("12.3") returns 1203 pence instead of £12.30 (1230 pence).
